chunks: My father and ‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Īsā, from his father, from Sayf ibn ‘Amīrah, from a man, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever does not visit the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) while he claims to be among our Shī‘ah, until he dies, is not among our Shī‘ah. And even if he is among the people of Paradise, he is from the visitors of the people of Paradise.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of visiting the grave of Imam al-Husain in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this hadith to establish Ziyārah al-Ḥusayn as a definitive marker of authentic Shī‘ī identity, distinguishing true adherents from nominal ones. The distinction between being a 'member' of the Shī‘a versus a 'guest' of Paradise highlights that while salvation may be granted, the fullness of spiritual belonging and intimacy with the Ahl al-Bayt is contingent upon this practice. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on Ziyārah not merely as a ritual, but as a continuous act of loyalty (walāyah) that solidifies one's place within the spiritual community.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 3. My father and ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain both narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from his father, from Sayf ibn ‘Amīrah, from someone who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:

Those who think they are among our Shia but do not go to (the Ziyārah of) the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) before their death, are not from among our Shia. And even if they are among those who enter Paradise, they will be (treated) as visitors in Paradise.
